html:
Four books of short Latin poems by Horace. The first three were published together in 23 BCE and the fourth in 13 BCE.

Horace set out to do in Latin what Greek poets such as Sappho and Alcaeus had done in their lyric verse, using their difficult metres. His odes cover wine, friendship, love, the shortness of life, the countryside, and Rome under Augustus.

Several lines became proverbs:

  • "carpe diem", seize the day;
  • "dulce et decorum est pro patria mori", it is sweet and fitting to die for one's country, which Wilfred Owen turned bitterly against the First World War;
  • "I have built a monument more lasting than bronze", about the poems themselves.

Horace was the son of a freed slave. He fought for Brutus at Philippi, lost his family farm, and was taken up by Augustus's friend Maecenas on the advice of Virgil. Maecenas gave him a farm in the Sabine hills, which he praises often. The Odes became a model for European poets for two thousand years.
sum: Four books of short Latin poems by Horace. The first three were published together in 23 BCE and the fourth in 13 BCE.
